implementation_corrections_made_before_m: Crump [0.1,0.9]: the overlap subsample (G=11, N=10800) matched Codex's exactly on the first attempt, but the point estimate did not (-0.0139 vs target -0.0064) because the first implementation used plain w_equal weighting on the restricted sample; corrected to weight by 1/p_hat (restricted to the same [0.1,0.9]-bounded values) times w_equal, consistent with Crump trimming being a robustness check on the SAME IPW estimator rather than an unweighted re-estimation -- after which the estimate matched exactly.

wild_cluster_bootstrap_extension.method_reconstruction_disclosure: final_result.json's method field is the string 'Rademacher one-step cluster-score bootstrap by economy' ('null-imposed cluster-score Rademacher' for Q3's two exposure contrasts) with no further documentation opened. Reconstructed as: draw one Rademacher weight per economy per replication (B=999), form the perturbed aggregate score X'(v(dot)u), take one Newton step from a FIXED bread matrix (X'DX)^-1 computed once at the original fit -- a one-step/score bootstrap avoiding a full refit per draw (Kline & Santos 2012-style). Q3's null-imposed variant builds u from a restricted fit (tested regressor dropped), per Cameron-Gelbach-Miller (2008) wild-cluster-restricted testing convention, while the bread matrix stays fixed at the unrestricted fit. Exact numerical agreement with Codex's own draws was never claimed or expected; comparison target is substantive-conclusion agreement.
